prompt:
You are a decision-support tool for a radiologist. Review this patient's frontal chest X-ray and report on six findings. A radiologist checks your output; give your best assessment.

Findings and their definitions:
- Lung Opacity: airspace opacity, consolidation, infiltrate or airspace disease in the lung. A discrete nodule or mass is not Lung Opacity (it is Lung Lesion).
- Cardiomegaly: an enlarged heart. A borderline or upper-normal heart size counts as absent.
- Atelectasis: collapse or incomplete expansion of lung tissue, including subsegmental or plate-like atelectasis.
- Lung Lesion: a nodule, mass or cavity in the lung. A calcified granuloma does not count.
- Pleural Effusion: fluid in the pleural space.
- Fracture: a fracture of the ribs, clavicles, spine or any other visible bone. Healed or old fractures count.

How to work:
1. Read the patient's image systematically first.
2. Then look at the 10 most similar cases from a reference database, listed below with their reports. They are other patients whose images look similar to this one. Use them as supporting evidence to confirm or question what you see in the patient's image, not as the answer: a finding in a similar case does not mean that this patient has it.
3. For each of the six findings, give its status (present, absent or uncertain), the probability (0 to 1) that it is present in this patient, the IDs of the similar cases that support your call (an empty list if none), and a rationale of one or two sentences. Then give a short impression. Do not explain what the findings are. Cite cases by their ID exactly as written, e.g. CXR316. Give the probability with two decimals as your honest estimate; for subtle, borderline or partly obscured appearances, use intermediate values rather than a fixed low value.

Similar cases (most similar first):
Case CXR3737 (similarity 0.891): FINDINGS: Heart size within normal limits. No focal airspace disease. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary findings.
Case CXR3793 (similarity 0.890): FINDINGS: No acute osseous abnormality. Scattered degenerative changes throughout the thoracic spine. Normal heart size. Tortuous and dilated aorta. Chronic interstitial markings. Left base opacity. No pneumothorax or pleural effusion. IMPRESSION: Left basilar airspace disease.
Case CXR733 (similarity 0.890): FINDINGS: There is a dual-lumen right internal jugular central venous catheter, the distal tip projects over the right atrium. There is no apparent pneumothorax. There is no focal lung opacity or pleural effusion. There is stable right upper lung lucency. The cardiopulmonary mediastinal silhouettes are stable. The visualized osseous structures appear within normal limits. IMPRESSION: 1. Distal tip of the dual-lumen right internal jugular central venous catheter projects over the right atrium. 2. No apparent pneumothorax. 3. Stable right upper lung lucency. CT chest may be helpful to further characterize.
Case CXR1049 (similarity 0.890): IMPRESSION: Comparison XXXX, XXXX. Well-expanded and clear lungs. Mediastinal contour within normal limits. No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality identified.
Case CXR2918 (similarity 0.888): FINDINGS: Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal. Pulmonary vasculature and XXXX are normal. No consolidation, pneumothorax or large pleural effusion. Osseous structures and soft tissues are normal. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary disease.
Case CXR700 (similarity 0.887): FINDINGS: The heart is normal in size and contour. There is a calcified granuloma in the right lower lung. The lungs are clear, without evidence of infiltrate. There is no pneumothorax or effusion. Osteopenia with mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine is noted. IMPRESSION: Stable appearance of the chest. No acute findings.
Case CXR1002 (similarity 0.885): IMPRESSION: Status post left mastectomy. Heart size normal. Lungs are clear.
Case CXR3852 (similarity 0.884): FINDINGS: Heart size is normal. No pneumothorax or focal airspace disease. No pleural effusion. Eventration of the right hemidiaphragm. Mild degenerative changes of the thoracic spine without fracture. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary findings.
Case CXR2276 (similarity 0.883): FINDINGS: This radiograph was XXXX available for my interpretation at XXXX hours XXXX/XXXX. There are low lung volumes with associated bronchovascular crowding and basilar subsegmental atelectasis. The cardiomediastinal silhouette and pulmonary vasculature are within normal limits. There is no pneumothorax or pleural effusion. There are no focal areas of consolidation. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.
Case CXR505 (similarity 0.881): FINDINGS: No focal consolidation, suspicious pulmonary opacity, pneumothorax or definite pleural effusion. Heart size and pulmonary vascularity within normal limits, visualized osseous structures appear intact. IMPRESSION: No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

The patient's frontal chest X-ray follows.
